_comments: THE RENEWAL ACTION (issue #243). Its own dot-json rather than an append to `.orders-actions.json`:
`filePattern` is `**/.*.json`, so MetadataSync reads every dot-json in this directory, and two
sessions each adding a file conflict on nothing while two appending to one file always conflict.
WHY AN ACTION AT ALL, when `Orders.SpawnRenewals` is already a remote operation. The operation is
the API a browser calls, and renewals have no browser — the term expires whether or not anyone
opens the app. The caller this needs is a scheduled job, and MJ's scheduler dispatches Actions and
Agents; no driver takes an operation key. This row is that adapter, and the class behind it holds
no renewal logic — see the header of `spawn-renewals.action.ts`.
SAFE TO SHIP `Active`, because Active describes the Action and not a schedule. Nothing invokes it
until the ScheduledJob in `metadata/scheduled-jobs/` is enabled, and that job ships Disabled and
configured for Preview. Running the Action by hand with no params is also safe: it places only
what is already due, and the operation's two idempotency guards mean a second run is a no-op.

fields.Name: Spawn Renewals
fields.Description: Place the renewal orders that are due: subscriptions whose latest term expires inside their own lead window and whose holder consented via AutoRenew. Runs the Orders.SpawnRenewals operation, which carries the selection, the booking path and both idempotency guards — this Action only reads parameters and reports the result. Preview returns the list without placing anything.
fields.UserPrompt: Place the subscription renewal orders that are due, or preview what would be placed.

fields.Name: AsOfDate
fields.Description: Treat this date as "today" when deciding what is due (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit for the actual today, which is what the schedule uses. A value that cannot be parsed is refused rather than replaced with today: today is the wrong answer most likely to look right, and on a live run it bills the wrong quarter.

fields.Name: Preview
fields.Description: True reports what WOULD be placed and writes nothing; false (the default) places the orders. A value that is neither is refused rather than guessed — the wrong guess bills customers. Note that a scheduler stores params as text, so "false" arrives as a string and is read as false, not as a truthy value.

fields.Name: MaxCount
fields.Description: Cap on orders placed in one pass. The safety valve for the first live run, where a mis-set lead time would otherwise invoice an entire book of business at once. Capped runs are not lost work — the subscriptions left over are still due on the next pass.

fields.Name: SubscriptionID
fields.Description: Restrict the pass to one subscription, for a targeted retry after a failure. Takes the Subscription row's ID, not its SubscriptionNumber. Omitted by the schedule, which considers every subscription.

fields.Name: Placed
fields.Description: How many renewal orders this pass actually placed. Always 0 on a preview.

fields.Name: Skipped
fields.Description: How many due subscriptions were passed over — already renewed, previewed, or failed. Each one's reason is on its entry in Candidates.

fields.Name: CandidateCount
fields.Description: How many subscriptions were due as of the run date, placed or not. Zero on a healthy day with nothing expiring; zero every day means something is wrong with the lead-day configuration rather than with the customers.

fields.Name: Candidates
fields.Description: Every subscription considered due, with the lead days applied, the expiring term's end date, and either the order placed or the reason it was skipped. This list is the deliverable of a preview run — it is what a person confirms before the job is allowed to place anything.
